_comment: DAY-STATE gate, spent branch only, calibrated specifically for T (T-Bank) — this grid is wider than the root data/params/rsi_pullback/cal_day.json. Forces UseDayATRGate=1 and freezes FreshDayATR=0, which permanently disables the 'day barely started' branch (dayStateOK requires fresh > 0), then sweeps SpentDayATR together with the entry shape (RSILower, RSIPeriod) and the exit band RSIUpper (1680 evaluations — about 4x the cost of a full grid.json run (409), because this grid crosses SpentDayATR x RSILower x RSIPeriod x RSIUpper instead of one narrower phase): entry is allowed once the day's range is already over SpentDayATR*dailyATR (the day is spent). Lowering SpentDayATR widens the late-entry window. Beware: the day-state gate covers two DIFFERENT strategies sharing one code path (early trend entry vs mean-reversion after a sell-off), and this file measures only the second one — isolating the first would take a separate config with SpentDayATR pushed far out of reach (e.g. 99) instead of FreshDayATR frozen at zero. The UseDayATRGate=0 control point lives in cal_screen.json. Run: go run ./cmd/backtest -ticker T -strategy rsi_pullback -interval Minutes30 -calibrate data/params/rsi_pullback/t/cal_day.json -out ./reports/T_day -months 24 -min-trades 20 -test-months 6 -metric profit_factor.
